gaps.sentence: We had a ___ view of the coast from the plane (SPECTACLE).
gaps.explanation: The adjective of 'spectacle' is spectacular; it modifies the noun 'view'.

gaps.sentence: ___ , the fire brigade arrived within minutes (LUCKY).
gaps.hint: sentence adverb needed at the start (-ly)
gaps.explanation: A sentence adverb comments on the whole statement: Luckily. The adjective 'lucky' cannot start the sentence.

gaps.sentence: After the fire, the theatre had to be completely ___ (BUILD).
gaps.hint: build again after destruction (re-); past participle needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rebuilt. The passive needs the past participle after 'had to be'.

gaps.sentence: There are many ___ (SIMILAR) between the two languages.
gaps.explanation: 'Many' needs a plural countable noun: similarities (note the -ty to -ties spelling).

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.
After 'an important' a noun is needed: discovery (note the change from -er to -y).

gaps.sentence: The island is ___ , with no permanent residents (HABIT).
gaps.explanation: 'No permanent residents' shows the negative: uninhabited (un- + inhabited). An adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.
